_comment: 🎒️ ZIP 2.0/✳️iso21320's own contribution to the repository test platform: the `zip` reference implementation registered for THIS subset's own 8-kind `ZipIso21320Mutation` vocabulary, and a comparison profile that — unlike the sibling `✳️base` one — checks the ISO/IEC 21320-1 constraints the profile exists to enforce.

oracles.rationale:
🩹️ RECLASSIFIED (ticket SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION, shard A10, 2026-09-02). This entry was registered `third-party-library` on the strength of a real crate that does genuine codec work, but the mutation's expected RESULT is computed by this owner's own `🦀️oracle.rs` -- its dispatch function's catch-all arm is `"mutation kind {...} has no oracle implementation"`, proof that every OTHER arm is an implementation, not a reading. Both halves of the comparison then descend from the same specification, so a shared misreading produces two agreeing wrong answers -- the one failure a differential oracle exists to catch. This is a `cross-semio-implementation`: a required SUPPLEMENT (metamorphic/inverse/round-trip evidence), never a substitute. A qualifying third-party reference for the mutation semantics is still owed. See $TICKET/📓️a10-oracle-honesty.md.

The reference ZIP reader/writer of the Rust ecosystem, and the only producer in this comparison that can honour a per-member compression method: ZipWriter::start_file takes the method explicitly, and ZipFile::compression/encrypted expose on read exactly the two wire properties ISO/IEC 21320-1 §4.1 and §4.4 constrain. That is what makes it the right independent reference for this subset rather than for ZIP in general. A distinct id and capability from both the plugin-level `zip` entry (zip-archive: plain create/read/remove evidence) and the sibling `✳️base` entry (zip-2-0-mutate): a mutation vocabulary belongs to the subset that declares it, and reusing an approved oracle outside its surveyed capability fails the contract's oracle-capability-mismatch check.

comparisonProfiles.description: ISO/IEC 21320-1 archives compared as a SET of members by name, uncompressed size and content digest, plus the archive-level comment as a normative field, plus the two ISO/IEC 21320-1 predicates per member: isoCompressionAllowed (the wire compression method is Stored or Deflate, §4.4) and encrypted (§4.1 forbids it). The predicate and not the method: §4.4 admits BOTH Stored and Deflate, so which of the two a writer picks for a given member is writer freedom — comparing the method itself would compare this repository's own canonical_compression_method policy against a copy of that policy planted in the oracle, which is the exact failure this platform exists to prevent. Entry order, compression level, timestamps, attributes and the extra field remain writer freedom as in the base archive profile.
